claim: Experts asked to describe a procedure unprompted omit most decision and knowledge steps (about 50-73% by step type). Prompted CTA probing recovers part of it (44% to 66% of steps in one study) but about a third stays missing.
agent_test: Ask the agent to summarise a solved hard case unprompted vs with 3 CDM-style probes (cues, alternatives, what a novice misses). Score both against a gold step list built from the full trace, at equal tokens. Evidence is two papers from one lab (Clark/Sullivan; N=3 and N=1 in key arms), so counted as one source.

claim: CTA-based training beats conventional training for surgical trainees on knowledge and technical performance, but effect sizes (SMD 1.4-2.1) are almost certainly inflated by small trials, weak controls and undocumented CTA methods. Expect much smaller effects elsewhere.
agent_test: Compare lessons mined by CTA-style probes vs equal-length plain-structure lessons vs no lesson, at equal tokens, on held-out hard cases. Do not plan power on g>1.

claim: The CTA benefit disappears for learners without a base: medical students show no gain on technical performance; only trainees gain. Tutor CoPilot shows the opposite split by tutor quality (largest gains for weakest tutors), so the base needed is topic grounding, not general skill. Gap search: SkillsBench (d05) saw a small model with curated skills (34.9%) beat stronger no-skill baselines, so a strong-model-only gate is not general; it may be specific to open-ended judgement tasks like tutoring.
agent_test: Run the same expert-cue lessons on a strong and a weak base model; expect gain mainly where the model can ground the cue. Gate lesson use by model strength.

claim: A CTA-derived decision model in the prompt (infer error, pick strategy, pick intention) raised GPT-4 tutoring quality sharply (overall 0.83 vs 0.51; +76% prefer) but not Llama-2 (0.49 vs 0.53) and only partly GPT-3.5 (0.45 vs 0.28).
agent_test: Add a notice-strategy-intention step before the answer at equal tokens; compare with a same-length neutral planning step. All Bridge evidence is one paper (4 experts, 40 pairs per model, expert arm uses gold labels).

claim: Structure must match the case: random decisions in the Bridge format made GPT-4 worse than no decisions (0.26 vs 0.51), so a lesson library needs retrieval or selection that fits the case.
agent_test: Inject random-but-well-formed lessons vs matched lessons vs none; confirm random lessons do not help and may hurt.

claim: A strong model's own self-chosen decisions equal expert decisions in Bridge for GPT-4 (0.84 vs 0.83) but collapse for GPT-3.5 (0.16, below none 0.28). LLM decision paths are less diverse than expert paths (entropy 3.37 vs 6.00).
agent_test: Compare self-elicited vs externally written lessons for the agent; measure strategy diversity of chosen paths.

claim: A deployed scaffold built from the Bridge expert-decision method raised real student mastery in a preregistered RCT: +4 percentage points (62% to 66%, p<.01), +9 pp for students of lower-rated tutors, about $20 per tutor per year. Estimated test-score effect is small (about 0.024 SD).
agent_test: Expect biggest gains on the weakest configurations of the agent; report effects split by baseline strength.

claim: CTA studies in medicine are mostly cheap qualitative descriptions of routine events; few test a downstream lesson, and rare events are under-covered (3 of 81 articles).
agent_test: When mining lessons from agent traces, deliberately sample rare and failed cases rather than typical successes.

claim: Experts differ from novices in strategies, pitfalls and links between steps, not in the count of decision points or factors; action probes discriminate less than cue and priority probes.
agent_test: Store lessons as cue, strategy and pitfall triples with cross-links; ablate links and pitfalls and compare.

claim: Scenario training built from CTA (ShadowBox) raises match to an expert panel when expert rankings and reasons are shown after the trainee commits: Marines N=59 .59 vs .44 (d=.63); soldiers d=.38 with no control; fire officers 86.9 vs 73.6. Outcome is expert agreement, not job performance, and authors evaluated their own method.
agent_test: Let the agent commit to a ranked cue list on a held-out case, then show expert reasons; test whether committing first beats reading the reasons directly, at equal tokens.

claim: Retrospective reports are partly reconstruction (Nisbett and Wilson), which is why CDM anchors on a concrete incident with short delay. Evidence read supports concreteness (props, video, eye-tracking replay help recall), but the founding paper and the Ericsson-Simon rebuttal were not opened. Gap search: LLM self-explanations are also unreliable. Models fail to name the cue that changed their answer (accuracy drops up to 36% with unmentioned bias; reasoning models verbalise a used hint only 25% to 39% of the time; larger models were less faithful in one 2023 study). Verify stated cues by removal.
agent_test: Ask the agent for the reason behind a past action with and without replaying its trace; verify the stated cue by counterfactual removal.

claim: Themes from CDM interviews saturate early (code saturation after interview 7, none new by 10 in the ICU study) and coding reliability is only moderate (Fleiss kappa 0.64). Gap search: for curated lessons in agents, 2-3 skills per task gave +19.0 pp and 4 or more gave +10.1 (SkillsBench), so the saturation point may be about 2-3 lessons per task; no interview-count saturation sweep exists for agent traces.
agent_test: Mine lessons from 7-10 failed cases per task type and track new lesson clusters per added case.

claim: No measured study was found where an LLM runs a full CDM or CTA interview and its output is scored against expert knowledge. Closest are human-run CTA with LLM use (Bridge), model interviewers on non-expert topics (GATE, AI Conversational Interviewing), and agent self-lesson mining. Gap search added: Wray 2024 (LLM analyst agent on puzzles, no scoring, 3 USD) and Data Therapist 2025 (GPT-4 interviewer, N=8 experts, 58-71% annotation overlap with a human interviewer). Still no CDM-on-own-failures test.
agent_test: Small in-house test: LLM-run CDM sweeps on the agent's own failed traces, scored by blind expert review against human-run sweeps.

claim: LLM interviewers under-probe: 88% of violations of the follow-up-on-unclear-answers rule came from the AI, and prompt edits broke behaviour that worked in pretests. Learned question asking is tied to the simulated respondent (win rate 72% falls to 62-65% with other roleplayers).
agent_test: Rule-check any probing operator after every prompt edit; evaluate against several respondents.

claim: Machine-mined lessons from agent trajectories (including failures) match or beat hand-written routines on web and QA tasks, but results are task dependent and some methods fall below no-memory on some models (AWM 40.8 vs 41.7 on Claude-3.7-sonnet). Gap search: failures added 3.2 pp to ReasoningBank (46.5 to 49.7) but AWM fell 44.4 to 42.2 when given failures; self-authored skills fell 8.1 to 11.5 pp below no skills in SkillsBench.
agent_test: Test each lesson on its own regardless of source; include failure-derived lessons; check the store does not fall below no-memory on the target model.

claim: Role labels do not substitute for expert content: persona prompts did not improve factual accuracy on average (162 personas, 4 model families, 2,410 questions); ExpertPrompting reports gains judged by GPT-4 only; clinician reasoning-mode templates did not raise GPT-4 accuracy and hurt GPT-3.5.
agent_test: Include a role-label-only control arm whenever testing expert-derived lesson content.

claim: Automated transcript-to-protocol parsing was weak before LLMs (span accuracy 38-47%, relation F1 74%) and no opened study measures modern LLM accuracy at it. Analyst variability is a known CTA reliability weak spot. Gap search: for applying a given codebook to interviews GPT-4 kappa was 0.97 / 0.75 / 0.56 vs human 0.97 / 0.83 / 0.63 on three tasks of rising difficulty; blind expert preference between human and LLM code sets was 51.5% vs 48.5%. Still no test on cue-action protocol building from CDM transcripts.
agent_test: Have the agent parse human-written CDM transcripts into cue-action steps; score against human-parsed protocols, with inter-analyst agreement as ceiling.

claim: RPD/CTA found that fireground commanders mostly recognise and run the first workable option rather than compare options (author-coded 80-90% of decisions; replications cited from military, firefighter, offshore oil studies). The count is the model author's own coding and the founding 1986/1989 papers were not opened.
agent_test: Compare retrieval of cue-pattern to action cases against an option-comparison scaffold on time-pressured tasks.

claim: Heavy CTA suits branching uncertain tasks; for linear procedures a streamlined pass may do, and time-limited CTA loses edge cases. No head-to-head on learning outcomes exists.
agent_test: Compare cheap vs deep lesson extraction on a branching task and a linear task.

claim: Lessons the agent writes for itself are not reliably useful, and agents often ignore condensed lessons. In SkillsBench self-generated skills scored 8.1 to 11.5 pp below no skills while curated skills added 18.2 to 24.8 pp. In Zhao 2026, corrupt, irrelevant or filler condensed lessons matched real ones in most settings. Contested: ReasoningBank and ExpeL report machine-mined lessons that help.
agent_test: In any lesson test, add a length-matched irrelevant-lesson arm and a self-written-lesson arm next to the expert-cue arm; check by trace that the lesson was read and cited.

claim: Failure-derived lessons add a small amount on top of success-derived ones when the extractor is built for them (ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7 on WebArena-Shopping, no memory 39.0) and can hurt when bolted onto a success-only method (AWM 44.4 to 42.2). No study compares failure-only with success-only lessons at equal count.
agent_test: Equal-count arms: failure-only, success-only, mixed, no lesson, across a strong and a weak model.

claim: LLMs approach human agreement when applying a given codebook to interview text, and fall as codes get more interpretive (GPT-4 kappa 0.97, 0.75, 0.56 against human 0.97, 0.83, 0.63). Agreement with one human understates LLM quality: blind expert preference was 51.5% human vs 48.5% LLM (Jaccard 0.30 vs 0.52).
agent_test: Score LLM-built cue-action protocols by blind expert pairwise preference as well as overlap with human analysts.

claim: No corrected effect size exists for surgical CTA training. The meta-analysis pooled four studies per outcome, ran no funnel plot or trim-and-fill, had I2 of 60 to 87%, and rated risk of bias 'some concern'. The SMDs 1.36 and 2.06 are upper bounds.
agent_test: Plan power for an effect far below SMD 1; treat any g above 1 in this literature as unverified.

claim: Open: no independent replication of Bridge was found, no CDM-reliability numbers from Hoffman 1998 or Klein 1989 were obtained, and no equal-length non-expert-content control exists in any CTA study. These three stay untested.
agent_test: Run the three-arm test (CDM lessons, same-format non-expert lessons, no lesson) at equal tokens on a held-out failure set.
